newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end sharply lower.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures ended sharply lower in brisk trade, yanked from early gains by weakening Treasury bonds.
Already nervous before key U.S. retail sales and inflation data midweek, bond traders took a weekly retail sales report late today as evidence of a very strong economy.

The latest Redbook retail sales survey showed sales up 0.9 percent in the August 9 week. U.S. July retail sales, due Wednesday, were forecast up 0.7 percent overall and up 0.5 percent excluding autos.
The monthly retail sales report will be released Wednesday, as will July producer price data. Consumer prices for July will be released on Thursday.
Traders said the afternoon rout was also tied to technical deterioration after September S&Ps were unable to sustain the day's earlier gains.
They noted sell stops below 930.00 and sell programs on the declines.
"It's not going to be pretty tomorrow," said Kevin O'Brien, a stock index futures trader with Prudential Securities.
"I would look for an immediate test tomorrow of 920.00 before we find any support," O'Brien said. "And I would not be surprised to break below that level."
He pegged another downside target at 911.00.
Others agreed that the market looked poised for more of a selloff. A drop below Friday's 926.75 session low would put September at the lowest price in almost three weeks.
"Those lows from Friday are very, very close," another trader said. He said September should test the Friday low sometime Wednesday.
Still, others noted that stock index futures dips are often met by good buying.

At the close, September S&P 500s were down 14.90 points at 927.65, KCBT Value Lines were 7.50 lower at 831.75, NYSE Composites were 6.95 lower at 480.85, Midcap 400s were 2.45 lower at 310.70, Russell 2000s were down 3.25 at 410.30, and Nikkeis were 55 higher at 19,015.
